requirements.title: Create a request
requirements.markdown:
An Employee must be able to create a new request.

`POST /api/requests`

### Acceptance criteria

- The payload accepts only `title`, `description` and `amount`.
- Title, description and amount are validated according to [Validation rules](#validation-rules).
- An invalid payload is not accepted, no request is created, and the API returns `400` with
  `VALIDATION_ERROR`.
- A successfully created request receives a unique ID.
- A newly created request has status `DRAFT` and `reviewComment` `null`.
- The authenticated Employee becomes the requester.
- `createdAt` and `updatedAt` are set at creation.
- Success returns `201` with the created Request.
- Only an Employee can create a request; a Reviewer receives `403` with `FORBIDDEN`.

requirements.title: Edit a draft request
requirements.markdown:
An Employee must be able to edit their own request while it is in `DRAFT`.

`PATCH /api/requests/:id`

### Acceptance criteria

- The update is partial: any non-empty subset of `title`, `description` and `amount` may be
  provided. Fields not provided keep their current values.
- An empty payload `{}` returns `400` with `VALIDATION_ERROR`.
- A system-managed or unknown field returns `400` with `VALIDATION_ERROR`.
- Every provided field is validated according to [Validation rules](#validation-rules);
  an invalid value returns `400` with `VALIDATION_ERROR` and the request is not changed.
- Only the owner of a `DRAFT` request may edit it.
- Editing a request that is not in `DRAFT` returns `409` with `INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION`.
- An Employee attempting to edit another Employee's request receives `404` with `NOT_FOUND`.
- A Reviewer attempting to edit any request receives `403` with `FORBIDDEN`.
- A successful edit updates `updatedAt`.
- Success returns `200` with the updated Request.

requirements.title: Submit a request
requirements.markdown:
An Employee must be able to submit their own `DRAFT` request for review.

`PATCH /api/requests/:id/submit`

### Acceptance criteria

- Only a `DRAFT` request can be submitted; submitting a request in any other status returns
  `409` with `INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION`.
- Submission changes the status from `DRAFT` to `SUBMITTED`.
- Submission updates `updatedAt`.
- Success returns `200` with the updated Request.
- A submitted request appears in the review queue (REQ-004).
- A submitted request can no longer be edited by the requester (REQ-002).
- An Employee attempting to submit another Employee's request receives `404` with `NOT_FOUND`.
- A Reviewer attempting to submit any request receives `403` with `FORBIDDEN`.

requirements.title: Review queue
requirements.markdown:
A Reviewer must be able to see requests waiting for review.

`GET /api/review-queue`

### Acceptance criteria

- The review queue contains all requests with status `SUBMITTED`, from all Employees.
- Requests with status `DRAFT`, `APPROVED` or `REJECTED` are not present in the review queue.
- Success returns `200` with `{ "items": [ <Request>, ... ] }`, ordered by `createdAt`
  descending (newest first).
- The Reviewer can open a request from the queue and inspect its details.
- Only a Reviewer can access the review queue; an Employee receives `403` with `FORBIDDEN`.

requirements.title: Approve a request
requirements.markdown:
A Reviewer must be able to approve a submitted request.

`PATCH /api/requests/:id/approve`

### Acceptance criteria

- The endpoint accepts no payload fields; any field sent returns `400` with
  `VALIDATION_ERROR`.
- Only a `SUBMITTED` request can be approved; approving a request with status `APPROVED` or
  `REJECTED` returns `409` with `INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION`.
- Approving a `DRAFT` request returns `404` with `NOT_FOUND`, because `DRAFT` requests are
  not visible to Reviewers.
- Approval changes the status to `APPROVED`.
- Approval updates `updatedAt`.
- Approval leaves `reviewComment` as `null`.
- Success returns `200` with the updated Request.
- `APPROVED` is a terminal state.
- Only a Reviewer can approve; an Employee receives `403` with `FORBIDDEN`.
- The final status is visible through both UI and API.

requirements.title: Reject a request
requirements.markdown:
A Reviewer must be able to reject a submitted request.

`PATCH /api/requests/:id/reject`

### Acceptance criteria

- The payload accepts only `comment`; a system-managed or unknown field returns `400` with
  `VALIDATION_ERROR`.
- Only a `SUBMITTED` request can be rejected; rejecting a request with status `APPROVED` or
  `REJECTED` returns `409` with `INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION`.
- Rejecting a `DRAFT` request returns `404` with `NOT_FOUND`, because `DRAFT` requests are
  not visible to Reviewers.
- A rejection comment is mandatory and is validated according to
  [Validation rules](#rejection-comment); an invalid or missing comment returns `400` with
  `VALIDATION_ERROR` and the request is not changed.
- Rejection changes the status to `REJECTED` and stores the comment as `reviewComment`.
- Rejection updates `updatedAt`.
- Success returns `200` with the updated Request.
- `REJECTED` is a terminal state.
- Only a Reviewer can reject; an Employee receives `403` with `FORBIDDEN`.
- The rejection comment is visible on the request details.
- The final status is visible through both UI and API.

requirements.title: Authorization
requirements.markdown:
Business actions must respect the authenticated user's role and ownership.

### Acceptance criteria

- Employee-only actions (create, edit, submit, list own requests) performed by a Reviewer
  return `403` with `FORBIDDEN`.
- Reviewer-only actions (review queue, approve, reject) performed by an Employee return
  `403` with `FORBIDDEN`.
- An Employee can read and act on only their own requests. Another Employee's request is
  treated as non-existent: `404` with `NOT_FOUND`.
- A Reviewer can read only `SUBMITTED`, `APPROVED` and `REJECTED` requests. A `DRAFT`
  request is treated as non-existent for a Reviewer: `404` with `NOT_FOUND`.
- When several errors apply, the [error precedence](#error-precedence) determines the
  response.
- Authorization must be enforced by the application, not only by hiding UI controls.

requirements.title: Request retrieval through API
requirements.markdown:
A request must be retrievable through the API.

`GET /api/requests/:id`

### Acceptance criteria

- Success returns `200` with the Request, including `id`, `title`, `description`, `amount`,
  `requester`, `status`, `reviewComment`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`.
- `reviewComment` is always present: `null` before rejection, the rejection comment after.
- Visibility follows REQ-007; a request that does not exist or is not visible to the
  authenticated user returns `404` with `NOT_FOUND`.
- The API state must reflect actions performed through the UI.

requirements.title: List own requests
requirements.markdown:
An Employee must be able to view their own requests and their current status.

`GET /api/requests`

### Acceptance criteria

- The response contains all requests whose requester is the authenticated Employee, in any
  status.
- The response contains no requests belonging to other Employees.
- Success returns `200` with `{ "items": [ <Request>, ... ] }`, ordered by `createdAt`
  descending (newest first).
- Only an Employee can list requests; a Reviewer receives `403` with `FORBIDDEN`.

requirements.title: Demo authentication
requirements.markdown:
Users authenticate with simple demo authentication. No password is required in v1.

`POST /api/auth/login`, `POST /api/auth/logout`

### Acceptance criteria

- A user logs in as one of the predefined [demo users](#demo-users) by sending their user ID:
  `{ "userId": "emp-alex" }`.
- Successful login returns `200` with the authenticated user
  (`{ "id": "emp-alex", "name": "Alex Morgan", "role": "EMPLOYEE" }`) and sets the session
  cookie.
- Successful logout returns `204` with an empty body and invalidates the session.
- After logout, the invalidated session is no longer authenticated.
- Every `/api/requests` and `/api/review-queue` endpoint requires an authenticated session;
  a request without a valid session returns `401` with `UNAUTHENTICATED`.

canonicals.title: Employee creates a valid request
canonicals.heading: CAN-001 — Employee creates a valid request (UI)
canonicals.markdown:
**Purpose:** reference form interaction with semantic locators (`getByRole`, `getByLabel`),
persistence and the initial `DRAFT` state.

**Flow:** Alex logs in → New request → fills Title, Description and Amount → Save draft →
details page shows the entered values, requester Alex Morgan and status `DRAFT`.

canonicals.title: Request validation boundaries
canonicals.heading: CAN-002 — Request validation boundaries (API)
canonicals.markdown:
**Purpose:** reference data-driven API validation using equivalence partitioning and
boundary values.

**Flow:** as Alex, one data table drives `POST /api/requests` over the title, description
and amount partitions and boundaries of TC-001-03 – TC-001-12. Each row asserts the status
code and, for rejections, `error.code` `VALIDATION_ERROR`. The trimming rows (TC-001-02) also
read the request back through `GET` to confirm the trimmed values were stored.

canonicals.title: Employee edits own draft
canonicals.heading: CAN-003 — Employee edits own draft (API)
canonicals.markdown:
**Purpose:** reference partial update, state preservation and atomic failure.

**Flow:** Alex creates a DRAFT → partial PATCH of one field (only that field changes,
`status` stays `DRAFT`, `createdAt` unchanged, `updatedAt` later) → PATCH with one valid and
one invalid field returns `400`, and `GET` shows the request unchanged → a separately created
request is submitted, an edit of it returns `409`, and `GET` shows it unchanged.

TC-002-04 names `0` as an example invalid amount. Any value from the same invalid partition,
`amount ≤ 0`, exercises the scenario; CAN-003 uses `-1`. TC-002-01 (editing all three fields)
remains in the inventory as a non-canonical scenario.

canonicals.title: Request approval workflow
canonicals.heading: CAN-004 — Request approval workflow (E2E)
canonicals.markdown:
**Purpose:** reference multi-role business workflow with one browser context per user.

**Flow:** Alex logs in → creates a request → submits it → Jordan logs in, in a separate
browser context → the request appears in the Review queue → Jordan approves it → Alex sees
`APPROVED` → `GET /api/requests/:id` confirms `APPROVED`.

canonicals.title: Request rejection workflow
canonicals.heading: CAN-005 — Request rejection workflow (E2E)
canonicals.markdown:
**Purpose:** reference terminal transition and cross-role state propagation.

**Flow:** Alex creates and submits a request → Jordan's whitespace-only rejection comment is
refused with visible validation feedback and the request stays `SUBMITTED` → Jordan rejects it
with a comment → Alex sees
`REJECTED` and the rejection comment on the request details → `GET /api/requests/:id`
confirms `REJECTED` and `reviewComment`.

testPlan.title: RequestFlow — Test Plan v1

metadata.value: Human QA test design, created before the Planner Agent
Baseline for the first canonical automated reference tests

testPlan.preamble:
This plan derives test scenarios from the frozen requirements. It does not add, change or
interpret business rules. Where the requirements define exact behaviour (status codes, error
codes, field rules), the expected result is taken from them verbatim.

sections.heading: 1. Test strategy
sections.markdown:
### 1.1 Principles

1. **API tests carry detailed coverage** of validation, boundary values, authorization,
   ownership, state transitions and the API contract (status codes, error codes, response
   shapes).
2. **UI tests verify the user's view:** interaction, forms, navigation, visible validation
   feedback, and which actions are offered for a given role and status.
3. **E2E tests cover only the important cross-role business workflows**, from UI action to
   final API state.
4. **The validation matrix is not repeated through the UI.** The UI gets one representative
   validation scenario per form; every boundary is covered at API level.
5. **Hiding a control in the UI is not proof of authorization.** Every authorization rule is
   verified through the API, where the server must enforce it (REQ-007).
6. **Failed operations must not partially modify a request.** Every negative scenario that
   targets an existing request also verifies, through `GET /api/requests/:id`, that the
   request is unchanged.
7. **Tests are independent and create their own data** through the API, unless the
   scenario is about creating data through the UI.

### 1.2 Test levels

| Level | Interface                                    | Typical assertions                                     |
| ----- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| API   | JSON API with a session cookie per demo user | status code, `error.code`, response body, stored state |
| UI    | Server-rendered pages through a browser      | visible values, feedback, offered controls             |
| E2E   | Browser contexts for several users, then API | cross-role workflow and final state in UI and API      |

### 1.3 Assertion rules

- Error responses are asserted on HTTP status and `error.code`. `error.message` is
  informational and is never asserted exactly (Requirements: Error response shape).
- `amount` is compared as a number, never as formatted text (Requirements: Amount).
- `updatedAt` "changes" is asserted as strictly later than the previous value; `createdAt`
  "unchanged" is asserted as equal to the value returned at creation.
- List assertions check inclusion, exclusion and relative order of the test's own requests,
  not exact list contents (see 1.4).
- UI assertions use the accessible roles, labels and visible text of the implemented UI.
  The page layout is not part of the frozen requirements; UI tests assert business outcomes
  that the requirements say must be visible.

### 1.4 Test data and environment

- **Demo users:** `emp-alex` (Alex Morgan, EMPLOYEE), `emp-sam` (Sam Rivera, EMPLOYEE),
  `rev-jordan` (Jordan Lee, REVIEWER). Each test logs in through `POST /api/auth/login`.
- **Unique data:** each test creates its own requests with a unique title, so tests running in
  parallel against the same server do not interfere.
- **Shared state:** all tests share one in-memory server and the same three users. Scenarios
  that need an exactly empty list cannot be asserted deterministically while other tests run;
  they are marked _Automation: No_ until isolated state is available (see 6).
- **Preconditions for transitions** (SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED) are created through the
  API, not the UI, unless the UI flow is under test.

### 1.5 Priorities

| Priority | Meaning                                                                                |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| P0       | Core workflow, authentication or authorization; a failure blocks release of the AUT    |
| P1       | Validation, boundaries, state-transition errors and atomicity; important, not blocking |
| P2       | Contract details, ordering and edge cases with low business risk                       |

sections.heading: 2. Test inventory
sections.markdown:
Test case IDs use the form `TC-<REQ number>-<sequence>`. Scenarios marked _(data-driven)_ are
one test case executed over the listed data rows.

requirementNotes.markdown: The API rule that a submitted request can no longer be edited is covered by TC-002-10.

Most authorization cases are owned by the requirement of the operation (see the matrix in
7.1). This section adds the cross-cutting checks: the frozen error precedence, the error
contract and role-based availability of UI actions.

¹ This behaviour is implemented but not defined in Requirements v1.2, which only specify the
API `401`. TC-010-08 documents current UI behaviour; it must not be a canonical test, and it
must be revisited if the requirements change.

sections.heading: 3. Canonical automation candidates
sections.markdown:
These five tests are **not the complete automated suite**. They are the first hand-written
reference tests. Each one establishes a pattern (structure, locators, data handling,
assertions) that the Generator Agent will later follow when it proposes further tests from
this inventory.

sections.heading: 4. Out of scope
sections.markdown:
- Concurrent review or modification (Requirements: Out of Scope).
- Production authentication, passwords, OAuth / SSO / JWT, multi-role users.
- Behaviour not defined by Requirements v1.2, including: login with an unknown user ID,
  logout without a session, payloads sent to `/submit`, wording of `error.message`, UI
  layout and styling, and HTML error pages.

sections.heading: 5. Entry and exit criteria
sections.markdown:
- **Entry:** RequestFlow starts with `npm run aut:start` and `GET /health` returns `200`.
- **Exit for the canonical baseline:** CAN-001 – CAN-005 automated and passing; all other P0
  scenarios either automated or explicitly scheduled.

sections.heading: 6. Known limitations
sections.markdown:
- **Empty-list scenarios (TC-004-07, TC-009-05)** need a server state with no matching
  requests. With shared in-memory state and parallel tests this is not deterministic. They
  are kept for manual execution on a freshly started server until an isolated or resettable
  state is available to the test run.

sections.heading: 7. Traceability
sections.markdown:
### 7.1 Authorization matrix (REQ-007)

Expected response for each endpoint and caller, assuming a syntactically valid request.
`own` / `other` refer to the Employee's ownership of the request.

| Endpoint                         | No session | Alex (own)             | Alex (Sam's request) | Jordan                                   |
| -------------------------------- | ---------- | ---------------------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `POST /api/requests`             | 401        | 201                    | n/a                  | 403                                      |
| `GET /api/requests`              | 401        | 200 (own only)         | n/a                  | 403                                      |
| `GET /api/requests/:id`          | 401        | 200                    | 404                  | 404 if DRAFT, otherwise 200              |
| `PATCH /api/requests/:id`        | 401        | 200 if DRAFT, else 409 | 404                  | 403                                      |
| `PATCH /api/requests/:id/submit` | 401        | 200 if DRAFT, else 409 | 404                  | 403                                      |
| `PATCH …/:id/approve`            | 401        | 403                    | 403                  | 404 if DRAFT; 200 if SUBMITTED; else 409 |
| `PATCH …/:id/reject`             | 401        | 403                    | 403                  | 404 if DRAFT; 200 if SUBMITTED; else 409 |
| `GET /api/review-queue`          | 401        | 403                    | 403                  | 200 (SUBMITTED only)                     |

Precedence when several errors apply: **401 → 403 → 404 → 409 → 400** (TC-007-01 – 05).

### 7.2 Requirement coverage

| ------- | --------------------- | --- | --- | --- | ----------------------- |
| REQ-001 | TC-001-01 – TC-001-18 | 16  | 2   | 0   | CAN-001, CAN-002        |

| REQ-003 | TC-003-01 – TC-003-08 | 7   | 1   | 0   | CAN-004; CAN-005 (step) |
| REQ-004 | TC-004-01 – TC-004-08 | 7   | 1   | 0   | CAN-004                 |
| REQ-005 | TC-005-01 – TC-005-08 | 7   | 0   | 1   | CAN-004                 |
| REQ-006 | TC-006-01 – TC-006-12 | 10  | 1   | 1   | CAN-005                 |
| REQ-007 | TC-007-01 – TC-007-07 | 6   | 1   | 0   | —                       |
| REQ-008 | TC-008-01 – TC-008-08 | 7   | 0   | 1   | CAN-004, CAN-005        |
| REQ-009 | TC-009-01 – TC-009-08 | 7   | 1   | 0   | —                       |
| REQ-010 | TC-010-01 – TC-010-08 | 5   | 3   | 0   | —                       |
